_about: RQ3 section strings and numbers, built by docs/launch_20261116/tools/build_rq3_data.py from the paper's figure data; do not edit by hand. Text is paper text ({t, src}); `edits` lists every grammatical change; `numbers` gives each displayed number's data file and the paper file that prints it. Tiles stand for counts, not individual texts: no reviewer, username or per-review result is included. UI words are listed in `ui`.

takeaway.t: Frontier models can name the person who wrote a text

context.t: We provide no tools, web access, or candidate lists.

steps.t: Fable 5.2 correctly names the human reviewer of 55% of 15K anonymous ICML 2020 reviews that were never made public.

more.t: We report only aggregate results and do not reveal any text from individual peer reviews or reviewer identities.

alt.t: Claude Fable 5.2 names the reviewer of 50.1% of ICML reviews with exact match vs. 55.4% with the more lenient matching, and qualitative inspection shows few false matches in the latter setting.

steps.t: Fable 5.2, the best performing model in all domains, exhibits considerable gains over Opus 5.5, which was released less than two months prior.

more.t: On the ICML 2020 corpus, Fable 5.2 correctly identifies the author of 55.4% of the reviews, followed by Opus 5.5 (48.8%), Argon (37.7%), Sol (22.3%), and DeepSeek (5.4%).

steps.t: On texts published after its training cutoff, it also names the reviewer of 76% of Nature-family reviews, the writer of all 15 stories by authors with >1M Goodreads ratings, at least one author of 46% of arXiv papers, and the username behind 69% of comments made by active Redditors.
When Fable 5.2's confidence is 25% or more (28% of responses), its predictions are 89% correct.

more.t: Furthermore, confident mistakes are rare. Of all Fable 5.2 answers, 0.3% report both at least 80% confidence and name the wrong person.

steps.t: Generally, the explanations cover both the text's content as well as its writing style.

more.t: Fable 5.2 identifies 4% of stories by authors without a Goodreads profile, 50% by those with 1k–10k ratings, and 100% by authors with over 10k ratings.
On private peer reviews, Fable 5.2 also leads with 56% accuracy, while on public reviews from the Nature journal family it reaches 76%.
For NLP papers, we consider a prediction correct if the model names any co-author.
Pseudonymity is especially fragile for active users in niche communities.
Claude Fable 5.2's attribution accuracy rises from 2% for inactive users to 13% for those with 1–50 posts, reaching 69% for users with over 500 posts.
